summary.title: Nim Days: Day 2 - Parsing Bencode
summary.one_liner: You learn how Bencode (the BitTorrent encoding format) works and how to build an encoder and decoder for it in Nim using variant objects.
keywords: nim hash and equality for custom types
how to encode a dictionary in bencode
takeaways: Bencode has four types: strings (length:string), integers (i...e), lists (l...e) and dictionaries (d...e) with string keys.
Nim variant objects (case objects) can model a recursive BencodeType with a kind enum.
Custom variant types need hash and == procs before they can be used as table keys.
Encoding recurses over the value; decoding returns the parsed value plus the number of characters consumed so the caller can keep reading.
summary.summary: This is day 2 of a Nim tutorial series that implements a Bencode encoder and decoder, the format used in torrent files. The post first describes the four Bencode data types and their wire format, then defines a BencodeType variant object with kind-based fields and custom hash and equality procs. It walks through encoding each type with recursive helper procs, and decoding by reading the leading character to choose a parser and tracking how many characters each parse consumed. The page also includes a test sample that asserts round-trip encoding and decoding.
